analysis.title: October 2026: First Look on Hedge Fund Performance and Positioning
key_insights: Global Fundamental L/S asset-weighted returns were -3.49% in October vs MSCI TR -0.77%, driven by both beta losses and negative alpha. YTD is +9.1%.

Systematic L/S returned -3.6% in October, the first time on the desk's record (since 2016) that both Fundamental and Systematic L/S fell 3% or more in the same month. It is the worst monthly drawdown for Systematic L/S since November 2020.
Fundamental L/S alpha was -1.75%, the worst monthly alpha since July and second worst in more than four years. Long side losses drove it, with short side losses to a lesser extent.
Largest Fundamental L/S alpha detractors were Volatility, China, Short-Term Momentum and Short Crowdedness. Gains came from the United States, Health Care and Size.
Asia L/S managers lost 9.4% in October, vs US L/S -1.9% and Europe L/S -0.5%. YTD figures are Asia +14%, Europe +7.8%, US +6.4%.
TMT L/S funds lost 12.6% in October (+5.1% YTD). Health Care L/S funds lost 1.4% (+8.5% YTD).
Equal-weighted average and median Fundamental L/S returns were -0.98% and -1.69%, so large managers underperformed smaller ones. YTD average is +12.25% and median +1.16%.

Systematic L/S loss was driven entirely by negative long side alpha. Short Crowdedness, Medium-Term Momentum and Asset Selection were the largest detractors, while Profitability, Earnings Yield and Growth offset partially.

Global equities saw the largest dollar net selling since March, with short and long sales roughly equal. Single stocks were net sold on risk unwinds, with long sales outpacing short sales 4 to 1, while index and ETF products were net bought (long buys outpaced short sales 1.6 to 1).
Info Tech, Industrials and Materials were the most net sold global sectors. Consumer Discretionary, Real Estate and Health Care were the most net bought.
US-listed ETF shorts rose 3% in October. ETF shorts are 10.5% of the US equity short book excluding index products, in the 18th percentile vs the past year and 1st percentile vs the past five years.

Overall prime book net leverage fell 4.2 pts to 73.4% (9th percentile one-year), the fastest decline since March, while gross leverage rose 4.8 pts to 314.5% (86th percentile one-year), driven by mark-to-market.
Global Fundamental L/S net leverage fell 3.2 pts to 49.2% (3rd percentile one-year), led by Asia L/S funds. Gross rose 4.2 pts to 210.7%.
North America was net sold for a second month, with short sales outpacing long buys 3.5 to 1. Its weighting vs MSCI World ACWI rose 2.1 pts to 15.2% underweight.

Europe was slightly net sold. Its weighting rose 0.7 pts to 3.5% overweight, a one-year high. DM Asia was modestly net bought (short covers outpaced long sales 4.2 to 1). EM Asia saw the largest net selling since July, with Taiwan, Korea and China all net sold.

US Info Tech saw the largest dollar net selling since June (long sales outpaced short sales 4.5 to 1), with all subsectors except Software net sold. Tech Hardware, Semis and IT Services led. US Info Tech long/short ratio is 1.71, in the 7th percentile vs five years.

Hedge funds rotated out of TMT and cyclicals into defensives. Defensives were net bought for the first time in 7 months, and US Health Care was net bought for the first time in 3 months, driven by short covering.
US Materials had the largest dollar net selling since May 2024. Its long/short ratio is 1.77, in the 1st percentile vs the past five years.

sector_views.rationale: Hedge funds were heavy net sellers, the largest since June, led by long sales in Tech Hardware, Semis and IT Services. Long/short ratio is 1.71, 7th percentile over five years.
Net sold for the first time in 4 months as short sales outpaced long buys 1.5 to 1. Diversified Telecom was the most net sold subsector, Interactive Media the most net bought.
Largest dollar net selling since May 2024, led by Chemicals, Metals & Mining and Containers & Packaging. Long/short ratio 1.77, 1st percentile over five years.
Net bought for the first time in 3 months, driven by short covers outpacing long sales 1.5 to 1. Biotech, Providers and Pharma were the most net bought subsectors.
Defensives were net bought for the first time in 7 months, with Staples net bought.
Little net activity, as long sales were offset by short covers, which points to de-grossing. Long/short ratio 2.01, 4th percentile vs the past year.

macro_indicators.interpretation: Global equity benchmark fell modestly while Fundamental and Systematic L/S funds lost 3.5% and 3.6%, so the hedge fund drawdown was much larger than the market's.
The US benchmark fell less than US Fundamental L/S managers (-1.95% total).

risk_factors: Short crowdedness and momentum factor reversals hit both Fundamental and Systematic L/S funds in October.
Asia and TMT exposure produced the largest drawdowns (Asia L/S -9.4%, TMT L/S -12.6%).
Gross leverage is at the 86th percentile one-year while net leverage and long/short ratios are near one-year lows, so funds are heavily grossed with thin net exposure.
vol_and_positioning: Overall prime book gross leverage is 314.5% (86th percentile one-year, 95th three-year, 97th five-year). Net leverage is 73.4% (9th percentile one-year).
Overall prime book long/short ratio fell 3.6% to 1.609, in the 7th percentile one-year and 2nd percentile five-year.
Global Fundamental L/S net leverage is 49.2%, 3rd percentile one-year, and long/short ratio is 1.610, 3rd percentile one-year.
US Fundamental L/S gross leverage rose 6.2 pts to 214.9% while net rose 1.4 pts to 47.1% (8th percentile one-year).
Europe Fundamental L/S long/short ratio is 2.218 (85th percentile one-year) and Asia Fundamental L/S net leverage fell 21.6 pts to 40.9%.
Short Crowdedness was a top alpha detractor for both Fundamental and Systematic L/S in October.

US long/short ratios sit at low percentiles: Info Tech 1.71 (20th one-year), Comm Svcs 2.73 (5th one-year), Consumer Discretionary 2.01 (4th one-year), Materials 1.77 (3rd one-year), Health Care 2.40 (6th one-year).
